t.d: Vegetable-tanned leather hand-cut and hand-stitched into poufs and other goods.
t.tech: vegetable tanning with plant tannins; hand cutting; stitched embroidery on the top panel; hand assembly
ctr: Fez tanneries (Chouara, Sidi Moussa, Ain Azliten)
t.auth: supple leather with grain variation; slightly irregular hand stitching; embroidery stitched through, not printed

t.r: Arabian Peninsula (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Oman, Qatar, Yemen)
t.d: Reception room where guests sit on cushions lining the walls, on the floor or a raised shelf; inscribed by UNESCO as intangible heritage in 2015.
t.tech: Floor seating of cushions and rugs; carved plaster (jis) and painted (al-Qatt al-Asiri) room decoration

t.d: Simplified, comfortable middle-class furniture after the Empire style.
t.tech: clean-lined veneered case work, coil-sprung upholstery
t.mat: cherry, ash, oak, fruitwoods, maple and bird's-eye maple veneer
t.auth: Local light woods rather than mahogany; earlier (1815–30) severe neoclassical, later (1830–48) British-influenced.

t.d: Veneering of case furniture in tortoiseshell inlaid with brass and pewter, perfected at the court of Louis XIV.
t.tech: marquetry inlay of metal into tortoiseshell

t.d: Italian marriage chests painted, gessoed, gilded or carved.
t.tech: gesso and pastiglia relief, panel painting, gilding, inlay, carving
t.auth: Many surviving cassoni are 19th-century neo-Renaissance pieces made for dealers such as Bardini and Volpi.

t.r: Indian subcontinent (Pakistan, north and central India, Bihar), Afghanistan, Myanmar
t.p: attested from 2nd century BC; described by Ibn Battuta in the 1300s
t.d: Hand-built bed frame of four legs and four rails, laced with a rope surface that can be retensioned.
t.tech: diagonal (bias) weave; short end laced to the foot rail (badaan) to adjust tension
t.mat: wooden legs and rails; munj, cotton or date-leaf rope; modern plastic tape and metal
t.auth: wooden paaga legs and iss/upala rails jointed without a fixed platform; hand-laced natural-fibre webbing with a tensioning end

t.p: recorded from the 1890s; revival in the 20th century
t.d: Damascus workshops making tables, pedestals and other furniture inlaid with mother-of-pearl and bone.
ctr: Straight Street and the old-town sūq, Damascus
t.auth: Revival pieces copy museum prototypes and 1897 Paris exhibition catalogues and mix old and new designs; check provenance.

t.d: Inlaid work in dense local thuya wood, prized for its burl, made in small workshops under the ramparts.
t.tech: channel-cut inlay tapped flush, finished with spirit, gum arabic and linseed oil
t.mat: thuya, ebony, walnut, citrus wood, mother-of-pearl, metal threads, camel bone
ctr: Skala de la Ville woodworkers' souk
t.auth: Geometric schemes with limited tree, vine and flower imagery; thuya is endangered, so plantation timber is used.

t.d: Swedish neoclassical furniture, often painted pine in pale colours.
t.tech: painted finishes in pale whites, blues, greens and greys; straight backs, tapered legs
t.auth: Early (1772–85) versus late (1785–1810) square undecorated legs; modern reproductions use cheaper materials.

t.p: carved ornament from at least 1560 (Mantingan Mosque); export industry today
t.d: Carved teak furniture from Jepara regency, whose characteristic motifs the regency patented in 2009.
t.auth: Motifs such as lung-lungan tree patterns and Mantingan Mosque ornaments; 99 motifs registered by the regency.

t.d: Carved walnut wood furniture and objects from Kashmir, protected as a geographical indication.
Front-opening Korean chests whose regional styles are read from their metal fittings.
t.tech: frame-and-panel chest with drop-front, cut-work metal fittings
t.mat: zelkova, elm, pine, persimmon veneer; iron, yellow and white brass
t.auth: Hand-forged fittings in good condition; region shown by metal type, motifs and hinge forms.

t.r: Mashriq (Egypt, Iraq, Levant, Hejaz); also Tunisia, Malta
t.p: 12th century (Abbasid Baghdad) onward; widespread in the Ottoman period, revived today
t.d: Wooden latticework of small balusters assembled into geometric patterns, used for screening windows and spaces for privacy and ventilation.
t.tech: balusters assembled into lattice patterns (hexagonal, kanaysi, maymoni, cross, sahrigi)
t.mat: carved and shaped wood; sometimes stained glass

t.d: Classical Chinese hardwood furniture, simple in form under the Ming and heavier and more decorated under the Qing.
t.tech: glueless, nail-free joinery: mortise and tenon, three-way mitred corners, frame-and-panel, yoke-and-rack
t.auth: species of wood, joinery without glue or nails, period construction details

t.r: United States (New England, New York, Kentucky)
t.d: Plain, functional furniture made by Shaker communities, including ladder-back and rocking chairs.
t.tech: turned posts, ladder backs, woven seats

t.d: Japanese mobile chests for clothing, trade and shipboard use, with strong regional styles.
t.tech: joined solid-wood carcases, forged or pressed iron and copper hardware, lacquer or dry clay-burnished finish
t.mat: keyaki, kiri, sugi, hinoki, chestnut, pine; iron, copper
t.auth: Hand-forged iron predates English pressed plate of the 1880s; regional lock-plate motifs (Yonezawa cherry blossom, Ogi four diamonds) and urajo locks (1860s) help date and place pieces.

t.d: Stick-built chairs whose legs and spindles are socketed into a solid carved seat.
t.tech: pole-lathe turning, steam-bending, adzed and scorped seats, wedged round tenons
t.mat: elm seats (England); pine, poplar seats, maple, oak, ash, hickory (America)
t.auth: solid saddled seat with socketed legs and spindles, splayed legs, worn original paint
